concepts.def: Declaration: there is no god but Allah, Muhammad is His messenger
Ritual prayer performed five times a day
Annual giving of 2.5% of surplus wealth to the poor
Fasting during daylight hours in Ramadan
Pilgrimage to Mecca, required once if able
Shi'a duties including Salah, Sawm, Zakah, Khums, Hajj

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Shahada is the first pillar — the Muslim declaration of faith.

'There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah.' Saying this with sincerity makes someone a Muslim.

Salah is prayer five times a day (Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha), facing Mecca. Shi'a Muslims may combine into three prayer times.

Zakah is giving 2.5% of surplus savings each year to those in need. It purifies wealth.

Sawm is fasting from dawn to sunset during the month of Ramadan — no food, drink or smoking.

Children, the sick, the elderly, pregnant women, and travellers are exempt. Fasting builds self-discipline and empathy with the poor.

Hajj is pilgrimage to Mecca in the month of Dhul-Hijjah, required once in a lifetime if a Muslim is able.

Pilgrims wear simple white ihram, circle the Ka'bah seven times, and stand at Mount Arafat.

Shi'a Muslims also follow the Ten Obligatory Acts — including Salah, Sawm, Zakah, Khums (a 20% tax), Hajj, Jihad, Amr-bil-Maruf, Nahi Anil Munkar, Tawalla and Tabarra.
